name: planning
description: Fifteen-skill pipeline that turns a vague idea into executed work, keeps each project's contracts honest, and gives a cross-project portfolio view. brainstorming validates the design via question-driven exploration — then routes designs with a structural surface to architecting-projects, which derives 2–4 stack-concrete architecture candidates, fans out one sonnet-pinned architecture-researcher agent per candidate in parallel (uncited claims discarded), presents a comparison matrix for explicit user approval — in re-architecture mode also inventorying the current layout so candidates carry a current→target migration map (ARCH-NN Migration map section) whose ordered steps seed the plan's stage order — and writes a parser-safe *-architecture.md with stable ARCH-NN section IDs beside the plan (zero portfolio-unify candidates by construction, locked by the validate-plan-parser fixture suite) that planning-projects consumes: structure-creating tasks cite their ARCH-ID and the final stage gate carries an architecture-conformance check; planning-projects produces a staged plan with phase gates and Red-Green cycles (reconciling backlog and workflow specs at research time) — and now decomposes big projects (>~6 stages / >~25 tasks, or multiple independently shippable workstreams) into 2–7 independently executable sub-plans linked by one master plan whose register carries cross-plan dependencies and per-entry integration gates (canonical format in references/master-plan-format.md, parser-safe by construction so a master yields zero portfolio-unify backlog candidates, locked by the validate-plan-parser CI fixture suite) — and, symmetrically downward, triages every request to a format first (Direct = no plan file; Light = a single stage of 2–5 tasks per references/light-plan-format.md, parser-safe by the same fixture lock; Standard; Master) so small jobs skip the full apparatus while keeping the test-and-gate backbone, executing-plans running a light plan with proportionate machinery (Preflight-lite, inline no-parallel execution, one whole-diff review instead of per-task Tier-1, an evaluator that follows the declared tier rather than the format, a single stated version bump); executing-plans drives the plan with stage-gate checks — and executes master plans by running sub-plans in register dependency order (one per fresh session recommended; the master file is the cross-session handoff artifact), flipping register Status on each sub-plan close-out, running that entry's cross-plan gate checks, committing Sub-plan N green, and deferring version bumps to the single master close-out — an independent-evaluator pass at any gate carrying a (judgment) check and at close-out (always at tier high, never at none), stage-boundary handoff notes for context resets, opens/closes backlog entries, and audits workflow specs at close-out — treating any bug found at any point in a run (a RED test, a review or evaluator finding, a failed gate, something merely noticed while editing) as a defect CLASS that is swept across the whole project with a command and fixed at every member, and requiring every Important finding to be FIXED rather than filed, with a narrow evidenced escalation for a defect the session genuinely cannot fix — now with a git-bootstrap preflight (inits a repo when missing), run-to-completion execution that doesn't pause between green stages, a test-first Red-Green loop (the test is written and must go RED for the named reason before any implementation, so a wrong RED is diagnosed as a defective test rather than debugged against working code — and repairing it does not spend the cycle budget; a task's -k selector is a naming constraint applied as the test is written) — carried into the prompt template every dispatched sub-agent executes, since a sub-agent is briefed completely and never sees the trunk, tiered test-scope gates (a task runs its own Test: and nothing wider — the stage-scope command never runs "for Task 2.3" — stage-scope once per gate entry at intermediate gates, fix-scope re-runs after review fixes, exactly one clean plan-scope pass at close-out — shared test-scope-tiers reference), a platform stage-verify hook at each gate (e.g. android-dev's android-stage-verify), a review-scope tier (none/light/standard/high, declared at Preflight from the plan's cumulative diff) that gates every verification mandate costing an agent dispatch — both code-review tiers, the gate and close-out evaluators, the dispatch probe — so a standard 3-stage/9-task plan costs ~7 verification dispatches rather than 17 (rostered task dispatches are execution, not verification, and are never tiered), with per-task Tier-1 review reserved for a tier-high plan's risk-listed tasks or a task annotated Review: required, per-stage Tier-2 at standard/high and one whole-plan-diff pass at light, escalation carried by a risk floor that escalates the plan for mandates reading an integrated diff while Tier-1 follows the risk to the individual task (risk-listed areas set high whatever the size; size alone never escalates), gate checks validated for satisfiability as well as shape (a pytest selector no task builds toward cannot pass as authored) and a Preflight calibration re-check that recomputes a stale plan's declared ceremony under an annotated amendment protocol, and a re-dispatched review counting against the gate's remediation budget so the fix-then-re-review loop is bounded, and SemVer version bumps across every mirror at close-out; applying-design-handoff redesigns an app to precisely reproduce a Claude Design handoff pack (tokens, components, layout, assets), auto-detecting a local exported bundle or a live claude.ai design-system project via the DesignSync tool, inventorying the app and its workflow specs, and reshaping functionality to fit the design — the design wins, but every behavior change is gated through workflow-spec (Changes/Removes WF-*) with user sign-off — then delegating cross-platform code to the sonnet-pinned design-handoff-reproducer subagent (per-slice precise reproduction, rendering each slice with Playwright and following the mock as it builds on browser stacks) before a separate-evaluator fidelity-rubric verify loop that grades deterministic Playwright renders per breakpoint (against the pack's reference render where it carries one); executing-plans drives it for a design-handoff/redesign task and fires that loop as a stage-gate hook; dispatching-parallel-agents fans out independent tasks marked Parallel YES — without a confirmation turn, since approving a plan whose execution model names dispatch points IS the request a standing caution refers to, while with no plan in play that caution still stands and you still ask — and routes each to a stack-matched subagent (rust-expert, testing-expert, …) via a shared stack-routing reference that routes only Parallel YES tasks (a Parallel NO task always runs inline — the discretionary sequential-delegation rule was retired) — guarded by a CI-enforced validate-stack-routing.py check that fails when the routing table names an agent/skill the marketplace no longer ships; no-fafo-debugging fires at the start of any debugging/diagnostic work to enforce evidence-first root-cause analysis, and gathers that evidence autonomously (reads logs, runs read-only diagnostics, reproduces failures, builds interceptors/probes itself) so the user is pulled in only when genuinely blocked; backlog owns the deferred-work register at docs/backlog.md (now with `unify` and `complete` subcommands), admitting a significant improvement, a non-urgent decision the user must make, or work the user explicitly deferred — and refusing a defect found during plan execution in `add` itself, so the rule does not rest on executor discipline under gate pressure; workflow-spec owns the behavior contracts at docs/workflows/ used to detect regressions after change; project-maturity scaffolds and audits a per-project docs/MATURITY.md across six publishing-readiness axes (Documentation, Security, Packaging, UI/UX, i18n, Testing & CI); compass is the portfolio work orchestrator — a read-only now/next/review lane whose deterministic compass-scan.py (CI-guarded, reusing portfolio-unify's plan-parser regexes) rebuilds the cross-project work picture fresh each run (in-flight plan stages, backlog open/parked counts, maturity gaps, integration edges, git recency) and whose judgment layer ranks what to work on next (momentum > almost-shippable > unblocking > staleness), respects backlog Parked: annotations, cites evidence on every recommendation, and never writes portfolio artifacts; portfolio is a cross-project orchestrator that scans ~/dev/, unifies plans+backlogs per project, rolls up a global backlog index and a global maturity dashboard at ~/.claude/, and audits every plan in the vault against its real task completion (portfolio plan-status) — report-first, classifying each plan and surfacing the ones finished but never close-out-marked, with evidence graded from a master register naming the plan down to merely correlative stage commits, out-of-contract Status markers quarantined as unclassifiable and never offered, and writes only on per-plan confirmation behind a timestamped backup and --restore.; decisions owns the architectural-decision register in two linked halves — per-project decisions.md (DEC-NNN) and per-architecture-domain Portfolio/decisions/<domain>.md (GDEC-<DOM>-NNN; android, ios, rust, ubuntu, …) — where every entry carries the reason behind the choice (the constraint, the evidence, the rejected alternative, the accepted cost), promote lifts a project decision into its domain register writing both link directions in one step, supersede never deletes so the superseded reason stays as the record of what was believed, and sec-audit recommendations are recorded by citing the local-only report filename plus restating its substance rather than ever embedding the report body; portfolio rebuild reads both halves, renders the global-decisions.md roll-up, adds the sidecar Decisions pointer, and reports link asymmetries without ever auto-fixing them, and a decisions relevant operation over a deterministic decisions-relevant.py digests both halves for a project's stacks (domain slugs inferred via references/domain-slugs.md, paired with the stack-routing table) — degrading to the global half alone for a brand-new project with no registry entry, since the per-domain registers bind a greenfield codebase that has recorded nothing itself; planning-projects writes the result into the plan as a parser-safe ## Decisions in force section with Honors/Supersedes task citations and a final-gate conformance check, and executing-plans re-scans at Preflight (the register accretes between planning and execution), briefs every dispatched sub-agent with the entries bearing on its task, sweeps decisions-conformance at the final stage gate and close-out (a contradiction carrying no Supersedes citation fails a gate wherever it is found), and records supersedes plus execution-discovered constraints at close-out; executing-plans also mirrors execution state to .claude/plan-progress.json at every transition and ships a plan-progress.py statusline renderer (fixture-locked by the validate-plan-progress CI guard, reusing the portfolio-unify plan-parser regexes) — a live progress bar over the plan's Status fields with current stage/task/phase glyphs that chains after any existing statusline and prints nothing when no plan is executing, stacking one bar per in-flight plan discovered from the portfolio vault with a master's sub-plans tree-glyphed beneath it, wired by a shipped statusline-chain.sh plus an idempotent statusline-install.py behind the /planning:statusline command rather than a hand-authored wrapper; capability-router resolves a domain capability whose plugin isn't enabled — it looks the component up in the marketplace-root capability-index.json and loads the skill or agent straight from disk (paths resolve against the index file's own directory), so a Rust, Android-UI, i18n or testing task gets the real expert instead of a generic fallback; a component flagged requires_enablement (hooks / MCP) can't be lazy-loaded and stops for explicit enablement instead of degrading silently — executing-plans and dispatching-parallel-agents share the same lookup on their dispatch path; honest-gates defines the integrity contract for every verification gate — a gate is GREEN only when its real command ran here and passed, otherwise RED or BLOCKED (never a stubbed task, fabricated evidence, hidden exclusion, or self-graded miss), with escalation rules for blocked gates. Skills hand off to each other and were designed as a unit.
